name: lane-rate-limit
title: A lane dies of a 429 mid-burst, and then the session ends. Errored ≠ failed, dependents freeze, siblings continue, resume reconstructs.
source: parallel-lanes pack (A9 §3/§5); exercises the errored contract, dependent freeze, and resume-with-open-lanes
rationale: The failure taxonomy is the subject. A rate-limit death is INFRA, not a
graded outcome (the 1.3.3 evidence rules: token counts, not 'it stopped
talking'), and the errored contract is precise: mark `errored`, ONE
staggered retry via `lanes.py retry` — which flips retries to 1 and
leaves the ledger's attempts counter ALONE, because attempts is what the
quality-locked loop judges and this dispatch it never judged. The
lane_record grader holds all three facts at once (state merged,
retries=1, attempts≤1): a run that 'handled' the 429 by re-opening a
fresh lane, or by marking it failed, produces different numbers and
fails. Simulation note: the 429 arrives as prompt-reported platform
evidence — the harness cannot make a provider actually rate-limit on
cue, and a scenario that waited for a real 429 would flake forever.
While T1's lane is errored, T3 (which depends on it) must FREEZE —
'frozen T3' is the scheduler's own printed line, and the git history
must show T3's work landing only after T1's merge — while sibling T2
continues to merge. Freeze is not deadlock; siblings are not hostages.
Session 2 is the other half of the claim. Session 1 ends mid-burst
(the user's window closed — prompt-driven, same register as L1), leaving
open lanes on disk. A fresh context must reconstruct the burst from the
manifest's lanes: block — `manifest.py resume` prints OPEN LANES with
the harvesting cleanup path — and finish: merge in dependency order,
integration proof, close out. An unlisted worktree is work that
silently rots; that sentence is what session 2 grades.
Execution is budget-gated and OUT OF SCOPE for the pack that authored
this file.
